transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because things at work don’t feel right anymore. The routing system at the warehouse—it’s not just a computer to me. I know it’s been tracking my moves and sending messages through the scanners, like it’s trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands there.
Have you actually heard voices or messages from the scanners, or is it more of a feeling that they're trying to communicate with you?

No, it’s not just a feeling. I hear them. Like even when I’m sitting out in my garage and everything’s shut off, I can hear dispatch voices clear as day. They’ll call my operator number and say I’m dangerous, or that security is coming for me. It sounds real to me.
Do you ever find it hard to follow your own thoughts or to express them to others?
I’m not sure. I mean, I can usually say what I’m trying to say, I think. Sometimes I lose my place when I’m upset, but I haven’t really noticed my thoughts getting tangled up or anything like that.
How long have you been hearing these dispatch voices?
It’s been going on for about a year and eight months now. Around then is when I first started hearing the dispatch voices and thinking the scanners were sending those messages.
Have you been acting in ways that are out of character for you since these voices started?

Yeah… I think so. At work, and sometimes even at home, I get so mixed up I’ll just stand there like my hands are still on the forklift controls. And I’ll repeat the same safety phrase over and over, even when people are trying to talk to me. That’s not really like me.
Do these voices and messages from the scanners and dispatch seem to be all part of one big story or plan to you?

Yeah. It feels like it’s all connected. The routing system at the warehouse isn’t just a computer to me anymore. I feel like it’s marking my moves, and the scanners are sending messages through it… like dispatch is trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one topic to another when talking, without really finishing your thoughts?
I’m not really sure. I don’t notice myself doing that much, but maybe other people would. I feel like I usually try to answer what’s being asked, though sometimes I lose track a little.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disorganized or hard to put into words when these voices are happening?

I don’t know if I’d call it disorganized. When it’s happening, it’s harder to get the words out cleanly. I can feel stuck or lose what I was about to say, but I’m not always aware of it in the moment.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other when these voices are not happening?
I’m not sure. When the voices aren’t going on, my thoughts feel more normal to me. I don’t really notice them being disconnected, but I might still get tired or lose my place sometimes.
When the voices are not happening, do you have trouble keeping your thoughts in order?

I’m not really sure. When the voices aren’t happening, it’s usually easier for me to think, but I can still get a little mixed up or lose my place. I don’t know if that means my thoughts aren’t in order, though.
When the voices are not happening, do you feel like your thoughts are disjointed or don't make sense to you?
Not really, no. When the voices aren’t there, my thoughts usually make sense to me. I might lose track a bit or need a second, but I wouldn’t say they feel disjointed.
When you're hearing the dispatch voices, do your thoughts feel like they're all over the place or hard to follow?

I’m not sure I’d say all over the place. When the dispatch voices are happening, it’s definitely harder to keep track of what I’m thinking, because I’m listening to them or trying not to. My thoughts can get interrupted, but I don’t know if they’re hard to follow in the way you mean.
Do you think your thoughts are still somewhat disorganized or hard to express even when the voices are not happening?

I haven’t really noticed that when the voices aren’t happening. I can still stumble over words sometimes or lose my train of thought, but I don’t think of it as my thoughts being disorganized. I’m not totally sure what would count as that.
Do you think your thoughts are ever disorganized or hard to express when you're not hearing the dispatch voices or feeling like the scanners are sending you messages?

I don’t think so, not really. If I’m not hearing them or feeling like there’s a message coming through, I can usually explain myself okay. I might pause or have trouble finding a word, but I haven’t noticed my thoughts getting disorganized on their own.
Do you think your thoughts are ever confusing or hard to understand for you or others when you're not experiencing any of these voices or messages?

Not that I can tell. When the voices or messages aren’t happening, I think I’m usually understandable. I might have to stop and think for a second, but I don’t feel like my thoughts are confusing in that way.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumbled or hard to make sense of when you're not hearing any voices?
No, I don’t really feel that when there aren’t any voices. I might get stuck on a word or have to think for a second, but it doesn’t feel jumbled to me.
Do you think your thoughts are ever confusing or hard to understand for others when you're not experiencing any voices or messages and just having a regular conversation?

I haven’t really noticed that, no. If it’s just a regular conversation and none of that other stuff is going on, I think people can follow what I’m saying. I might pause or lose my place for a second, but I don’t think it comes out confusing.
Do you think your thoughts are ever disorganized when you're not feeling stressed or hearing any voices?
I don’t think so. When I’m not stressed and I’m not hearing anything, my thoughts feel pretty normal to me. Maybe I pause sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it disorganized.
Do you think your thoughts are ever hard to follow or make sense of for you when you're not hearing any voices or feeling like you're receiving messages?

Not really, no. If I’m not hearing anything or feeling like there are messages coming in, my thoughts usually make sense to me. I might have to pause and gather myself, but I can follow what I’m thinking.
